setting.en: It's recess. A group is playing tag, and Sam is standing by the fence, all alone.

text.en: Walk over, say hi, and invite Sam to play with you.

why.en: Inviting someone who is alone shows them they belong. One kind hello can turn a whole recess around.

text.en: Ask Teacher Mae to help everyone find a game to join.

why.en: Telling a trusted adult is a good idea! Asking Sam yourself works even faster, because Sam feels included right away.

text.en: Keep playing. Sam will find something to do.

why.en: It's easy to keep playing, but Sam may still feel alone. A quick hello makes a big difference.

setting.en: In the hallway, someone makes a joke about Leo's lunch box, and a few classmates giggle. Leo goes quiet.

text.en: Don't laugh. Stand next to Leo, then go together to tell Teacher Mae what happened.

why.en: Standing next to Leo shows that nobody has to face this alone, and a trusted adult can help it stop.

text.en: Don't laugh, and quietly walk away.

why.en: Not laughing is a good start! Standing next to Leo, or telling an adult, would help even more.

text.en: Giggle a little so nobody teases you too.

why.en: Laughing along can feel safer, but it makes the joke seem okay and it hurts Leo. Next time, try not laughing and standing with Leo.

setting.en: After the trip, a classmate keeps whispering a nickname that Bea doesn't like. Bea asks for it to stop, but it goes on.

text.en: Tell Bea, "That's not okay, I'm with you," and go together to tell Teacher Dan.

why.en: Speaking up kindly and telling a trusted adult together gives Bea real support.

text.en: Sit with Bea at lunch and talk about something fun.

why.en: Being a friend helps a lot. Telling a trusted adult too means the nickname can really be stopped.

text.en: Say nothing. It's only a nickname.

why.en: A nickname someone doesn't like can still hurt, even when it sounds small. Next time, check in with Bea.

setting.en: Two captains are picking teams. Rico is the last one waiting, and a few classmates start to giggle.

text.en: Say, "I'll pick Rico!" Cheer Rico on, and tell Coach Ray if it keeps happening.

why.en: Choosing Rico shows everyone belongs on a team. Telling Coach Ray means the grown-ups can help make picking fair.

text.en: Don't giggle, and give Rico a friendly smile.

why.en: A kind smile helps! Choosing Rico out loud helps even more, because Rico gets a spot right away.

text.en: Look away and wait for it to be over.

why.en: Waiting can leave Rico feeling left out. Speaking up for a teammate is brave and kind.

text.en: Who has the poster paper?
LOL 😂

photo.en: A photo of Sam that Sam didn't share

setting.en: A photo of Sam shows up in the class group chat. Sam didn't share it, and the 😂 reactions are piling up. Sam goes quiet.

text.en: Don't react or forward it. Take a screenshot, block and report the account, and show a trusted adult.

why.en: A screenshot is proof, blocking stops more messages, and a trusted adult can really help. Not reacting keeps the photo from spreading.

text.en: Send Sam a private message: "That wasn't okay. I'm here for you."

why.en: A kind message can mean the world to Sam. A screenshot, a report and a trusted adult would help stop it, too.

text.en: React with 😂 so you don't stand out.

why.en: A reaction can feel harmless, but it helps the photo spread and hurts Sam. Try skipping the reaction and telling a trusted adult.

text.en: My group is meeting after lunch!
FORWARD THIS to everyone! 😂

photo.en: A meme making fun of Nico

setting.en: A meme about Nico is going around the chat with the words "Forward this to everyone!"

text.en: Don't forward it. Take a screenshot, report it, and tell a trusted adult.

why.en: Forwarding keeps unkind messages going. A report and a trusted adult help them stop.

text.en: Delete it and don't say anything.

why.en: Not forwarding is a good start! A screenshot and a trusted adult would help it stop for everyone.

text.en: Forward it. It's only a meme.

why.en: Memes about a person can hurt, and every forward makes them spread further. Next time, stop it with you and tell an adult.
